THE MEETING IS BROADCAST LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. FOR QUESTIONS OR ASSISTANCE, PLEASE CONTACT THE CITY CLERK'S OFFICE AT 949-724-6205, OR VIA EMAIL AT CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG. NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
2. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  REGULAR MEETING

  June 8, 2021

  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:07 p.m. on June
8, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll*
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. Mayor Khan also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout
City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to submit live
comments via Zoom and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments
on all agenda items, and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded
to the City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  June 8, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Kuo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Sheikh Atef Mahgoub, Religious Director from the Islamic Center of Irvine, provided the
  invocation.

  MOMENT OF SILENCE

  Mayor Khan requested a moment of silence in memory of those who lost their lives as
  a result of the recent shooting that occurred at a San Jose rail yard.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Agran noted his appreciation to staff for allowing the ability for him and
  members of the public to participate remotely in City Council meetings, and looked
  forward to returning to in-person meetings.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  The Movies on the Lawn series of family-friendly outdoor screenings at the
  Orange County Great Park will kick off on Saturday, June 26, with a showing of
  The War with Grandpa. The movie will begin after sunset at approximately 8:15
  p.m. Attendees are encouraged to bring a blanket or low-back chair and enjoy
  the film with friends and family from individual, socially distanced picnic circles.
  Movies will continue various Saturday evenings through August 21. Due to
  limited space available, these events are open to Irvine residents only. Admission
  is free; however, advanced registration is required at yourirvine.org. For more
  information, visit ocgp.org or call 949-724-6247.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  June 8, 2021

  •  The City of Irvine would like to remind everyone in the community to follow
  important water safety tips. Drowning remains the leading cause of injury and
  death among children under five, and among the top-five leading causes for
  those under the age of 18, both in Orange County and in California. The best
  way to keep children safe is to take a “layers of protection” approach, which
  includes: 1) never leaving a child alone near water, even for a few seconds; 2)
  making sure a supervising adult is close enough to touch the child under 4 years
  old near water; 3) making sure parents and child caregivers know how to perform
  rescue techniques in an emergency, and; 4) if a child is missing, check the pool
  first. The City encourages everyone in the community to take the time to learn
  more about water safety by visiting drowningpreventionoc.org.

  •  Through partnerships with local health care providers, more than 7,500 COVID-
  19 vaccines have been administered to members of the community. The City is
  proud to continue providing opportunities for residents to get vaccinated through
  drive-thru clinics at the Orange County Great Park and mobile clinics in Irvine
  neighborhoods. Over the past few weeks, clinics have been held at William
  Woollett, Jr. Aquatics Center, Portola Springs Community Center, South Coast
  Chinese Cultural Center, and Diamond Jamboree with more clinics planned. For
  more information about the clinic and to make an appointment, visit
  cityofirvine.org/vaccine. Vaccines are one of the most powerful tools to end the
  pandemic and keep the community safe. The City commends everyone who has
  received the vaccine and encourages everyone who can get vaccinated to do so.

  •  Irvine’s park system has been ranked 7th in the nation and 2nd in California by the
  nonprofit Trust for Public Land. This is the sixth consecutive year Irvine has been
  listed among the top 10 nationally in the annual ParkScore Index, which ranks
  the nation’s 100 largest cities based on factors including: park access, acreage,
  investment, amenities, and equity. In its ranking, the Trust for Public Land noted
  that 89 percent of Irvine resident live within a 10-minute walk of a park, an
  increase from the 2020 ranking of 82 percent. The importance the City’s parks
  have played in the community’s mental and physical health over the past year
  cannot be overstated and are one of the many reasons Irvine is an ideal home
  for families, children, individuals, and outdoor enthusiasts of all kinds. For more
  information about Irvine’s ranking visit tpl.org/parkscore; and to learn more about
  Irvine parks, visit cityofirvine.org/parks.

  •  Irvine was one of 487 cities recognized nationally last month as a Bicycle Friendly
  Community by the League of American Bicyclists for working to create safer
  streets and better bicycling for everyone. Irvine was recertified with a silver-level
  award, recognizing the commitment to bicycling and efforts to improve and
  innovate, ensuring that biking is safe and accessible to all. Everyone is
  encouraged to take advantage of the City’s bicycling network of 364 miles of on-
  street and off-street bikeways. To learn more about the City’s bikeways, visit
  cityofirvine.org/bikeways.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  June 8, 2021

  •  Late last Friday, June 4, the City received the California Department of Veterans
  Affairs cemetery feasibility studies for the golf course and Amended and
  Restated Development Agreement (ARDA) locations. City staff is reviewing the
  study summaries and asked CalVet to provide a public presentation of the results
  and next steps. Both feasibility studies can be reviewed on the City’s website at
  cityofirvine.org/veteranscemetery. For additional information about the Southern
  California Veterans Cemetery and to view supporting documents, visit CalVet’s
  webpage at calvet.ca.gov.

  2.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  Mayor Khan reordered the agenda to consider Council Business Item No. 2.2
  prior to Council Business Item No. 2.1.

  2.1  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE AND DIRECTION TO DIRECTOR
  OF EMERGENCY SERVICES ON RELEVANT ACTION ITEMS

  This item was considered following Council Business Item No. 2.2.

  Michelle Grettenberg, Assistant City Manager, presented the staff
  report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: suggesting that a plan be developed
  for a possible resurgence of the virus in the fall; reiterated that the
  COVID-19 Task Force was tasked with plan development in the event
  of a resurgence; suggested that updates be provided by the COVID-19
  Task Force meetings to the City Council; and inquired about ways to
  make outdoor dining a permanent option.

  There were no public comments.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, and
  unanimously carried by those members present (Councilmember
  Carroll absent) to:

  Confirm the continuation of all outdoor dining and other outdoor
  special event permits post-June 15.

  2.2  CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR STATE LEGISLATIVE
  ADVOCACY SERVICES

  This item was considered prior to Council Business Item No. 2.1.

  Michelle Grettenberg, Assistant City Manager, presented the staff
  report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether cost was a
  consideration during the evaluation process, and if the two firms that
  responded provided different pricing; questioned whether pricing
  submitted by the other responding bidder was confidential; inquired
  about any service level issues with the existing firm; and suggested
  quarterly updates to the City Council rather than twice per year.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that the City Council could direct
  staff to negotiate with another qualified bidder.
